standards.description: Utilize flexible counting strategies to determine and describe quantities up to 200, including skip counting and identifying even/odd numbers.

skills.description: Represent forward counting patterns when counting by groups of 2 up to at least 50, starting at various multiples of 2 using tools like objects, number lines, or hundreds charts.
Represent forward counting patterns when counting by groups of 5s, 10s, and 25s up to at least 200 using tools like objects, number lines, or hundreds charts.
Describe and use patterns in skip counting by multiples of 2 (to at least 50), and multiples of 5, 10, and 25 (to at least 200) to justify the next number in the counting sequence.
Represent forward counting patterns when counting by groups of 100 up to at least 1,000 starting at 0 using tools like objects, number lines, calculators, or one thousand charts.
Represent backward counting patterns when counting by groups of 10 from 200 or less using tools like objects, number lines, calculators, or hundreds charts.
Describe and use patterns in skip counting backwards by 10s (from at least 200) to justify the next number in the counting sequence.
Choose a reasonable estimate up to 1,000 when given a contextual problem.
Represent even numbers (up to 50) with concrete objects using two equal groups or two equal addends.
Represent odd numbers (up to 50) with concrete objects using two equal groups with one leftover or two equal addends plus 1.
Determine whether a number (up to 50) is even or odd using concrete objects and justify reasoning.

standards.description: Demonstrate understanding of the ten-to-one relationships of the base 10 number system to represent, compare, and order whole numbers up to 999.

skills.description: Write the three-digit whole number represented by a given model (e.g., concrete objects, pictures of base 10 blocks).
Read, write, and represent three-digit numbers in standard form, expanded form, and word form using concrete or pictorial representations.
Apply patterns within the base 10 system to determine and communicate the place (ones, tens, hundreds) and value of each digit in a three-digit whole number.
Investigate and explain the ten-to-one relationships among ones, tens, and hundreds using models.
Compose and decompose whole numbers up to 200 by making connections between models and counting strategies.
Plot and justify the position of a given number up to 100 on a number line with pre-marked benchmarks of 1s, 2s, 5s, 10s, or 25s.
Compare two whole numbers, each 999 or less, represented concretely, pictorially, or symbolically using words and symbols.
Order up to three whole numbers, each 999 or less, represented concretely, pictorially, or symbolically from least to greatest and greatest to least.

standards.description: Use mathematical reasoning and justification to solve contextual problems involving partitioning models into equal-sized parts.

skills.description: Model and describe fractions as representing equal-size parts of a whole.
Describe the relationship between the number of fractional parts needed to make a whole and the size of the parts.
Compose the whole for a given fractional part and its value for halves, fourths, eighths, thirds, and sixths.
Count by unit fractions up to two wholes using same-size fraction pieces from a region/area model.
Represent, name, and write fractional parts of a whole for halves, fourths, eighths, thirds, and sixths using region/area models.
Represent, name, and write fractional parts of a whole for halves, fourths, eighths, thirds, and sixths using length models.
Represent, name, and write fractional parts of a whole for halves, fourths, eighths, thirds, and sixths using set models.
Compare unit fractions for halves, fourths, eighths, thirds, and sixths using words and symbols with region/area and length models.

standards.description: Solve problems involving counting and representing money amounts up to $2.00.

skills.description: Identify a quarter and its value and determine multiple ways to represent the value of a quarter using pennies, nickels, and/or dimes.
Count by ones, fives, tens, and twenty-fives to determine the value of a collection of mixed coins and one-dollar bills whose total value is $2.00 or less.
Construct a set of coins and/or bills to total a given amount of money whose value is $2.00 or less.
Represent the value of a collection of coins and one-dollar bills (limited to $2.00 or less) using the cent and dollar symbols and decimal point.

standards.description: Recall addition and subtraction facts within 20 and solve single-step and multistep problems using addition and subtraction with whole numbers up to 100.

skills.description: Apply strategies (e.g., rounding, compatible numbers) to estimate solutions for single-step addition or subtraction problems.
Apply strategies (e.g., concrete models, place value, properties of addition) to determine the sum or difference of two whole numbers up to 100.
Represent, solve, and justify solutions to single-step and multistep contextual problems involving addition or subtraction of whole numbers up to 100.
Demonstrate fluency with addition and subtraction within 20 by applying reasoning strategies (e.g., doubles, near doubles, make-a-ten).
Recall with automaticity addition and subtraction facts within 20.
Use patterns, models, and strategies to make generalizations about algebraic properties for fluency.
Determine the missing number in an equation with addition and subtraction within 20.
Use inverse relationships to write all related facts connected to a given addition or subtraction fact model within 20.
Describe the not equal symbol as representing a relationship where expressions on either side represent different values and justify reasoning.

standards.description: Reason mathematically using standard U.S. Customary units to estimate, measure, and compare objects by length, weight, and liquid volume.

skills.description: Explain the purpose of measurement tools (ruler, scales, measuring cups) and how to use them appropriately.
Use U.S. Customary units to estimate, measure, and compare the length of an object to the nearest inch using a ruler.
Use U.S. Customary units to estimate, measure, and compare the weight of an object to the nearest pound using a scale.
Use U.S. Customary units to estimate, measure, and compare the liquid volume of a container to the nearest cup using a measuring cup.

standards.description: Demonstrate understanding of the concept of time to the nearest five minutes using analog and digital clocks.

skills.description: Identify the number of minutes in an hour (60 minutes) and the number of hours in a day (24 hours).
Determine the most appropriate unit of time (minutes, hours, days, or weeks) for a given activity or context and explain reasoning.
Show, tell, and write time to the nearest five minutes using analog and digital clocks.
Match a written time to the time shown on an analog clock to the nearest five minutes.

standards.description: Identify, describe, and create plane figures with at least one line of symmetry and explain its relationship with congruency.

skills.description: Explore a figure using tools (e.g., paper folding, geoboards, drawings) to show and justify a line of symmetry, if one exists.
Create figures with at least one line of symmetry using various concrete and pictorial representations.
Describe the two resulting figures formed by a line of symmetry as being congruent (having the same shape and size).

standards.description: Describe, name, compare, and contrast plane and solid figures.

skills.description: Trace faces of solid figures (cubes and rectangular prisms) to create the set of plane figures related to the solid figure.
Compare and contrast models and nets of cubes and rectangular prisms (e.g., number and shapes of faces, edges, vertices).
Given a concrete or pictorial model, name and describe the solid figure (sphere, cube, rectangular prism) by its characteristics.
Compare and contrast plane and solid figures (circles/spheres, squares/cubes, rectangles/rectangular prisms) according to their characteristics.

standards.description: Apply the data cycle to pose questions, collect data, organize and represent data, and analyze data with a focus on pictographs and bar graphs.

skills.description: Pose questions, given a predetermined context, that require the collection of data (limited to 25 or fewer data points for no more than six categories).
Determine the data needed to answer a posed question and collect the data using various methods (e.g., voting, lists, tables, charts, tallying).
Organize and represent a data set using a pictograph where each symbol represents up to 2 data points. Determine and use a key to assist in the analysis.
Organize and represent a data set using a bar graph with a title and labeled axes (limited to 25 or fewer data points for up to six categories).
Analyze data represented in pictographs and bar graphs and communicate results by asking and answering questions about the data.
Draw conclusions about the data and make predictions based on the data represented in pictographs and bar graphs.

standards.description: Describe, extend, create, and transfer repeating and increasing patterns using various representations.

skills.description: Identify and describe repeating and increasing patterns.
Analyze a repeating or increasing pattern and generalize the change to extend the pattern using objects, pictures, and numbers.
Create a repeating or increasing pattern using various representations (e.g., objects, pictures, numbers).
Transfer a given repeating or increasing pattern from one form to another (e.g., objects, pictures, numbers) and explain the connection.
